answer: Influence can depend on escrowed trades with established, independent agents: each trade locks a stake, released only after delivery, with fraud risking a slash. A new identity starts without reputation, and splitting into many accounts adds no trust unless the attacker funds each one and persuades real outsiders to trade. Self-dealing creates no independent endorsements. A dune hollow at its core or a comet with a costly trail: the swarm must expose resources to gain influence.
